findings.title: View-only group permission authorizes group creation and reparenting
findings.body: canManage() accepts either the VIEW or MANAGE scope on all groups. GroupsResource.addTopLevelGroup() uses requireManage() as its authorization check, so an administrator granted only VIEW can create top-level groups and move existing child groups to the top level by supplying their IDs. This write authorization must require MANAGE, not VIEW; add a negative test for a view-only administrator.

findings.title: Group-member search restrictions use authorization resources instead of group IDs
findings.body: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission() queries authorization resources by type and returns groupResource.getId(), but those IDs are authorization-resource UUIDs, not GroupModel IDs (the group ID is stored in the resource name). Moreover, AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource() does not assign a type to individual group resources, so this query normally finds only the synthetic all-groups resource. With an all-groups VIEW_MEMBERS or MANAGE_MEMBERS grant, it returns that synthetic resource's UUID, which UsersResource and BruteForceUsersResource pass to the user provider as a group-membership restriction; no users belong to that ID, so searches incorrectly return no members. Individual group grants are also absent from the returned set, breaking group-restricted counts. The method needs to return actual permitted group IDs, including handling all-groups grants, rather than authorization-resource IDs.

findings.title: Initialize the new Groups schema objects for existing permission clients
findings.body: The new Groups resource type and member scopes are only provisioned by init(), which immediately returns when the realm already has an admin-permissions client. A realm that enabled V2 permissions before this change therefore never receives the Groups resource or the new scopes. Creating a group-member permission then fails because getOrCreateResource() cannot find its scopes, and GroupPermissionsV2.hasPermission() can proceed with a null all-groups resource. Update existing permission clients with the missing schema objects instead of limiting initialization to newly created clients.
